newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - January 31.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Police arrest Tamil separatist rebel who was disguised as a fisherman, in Udappuva north of Colombo.
Senior Tamil rebel who was in chanrge of finances in northern Kilinochchi area, flees to India with jewellery worth one million rupees.
Main opposition United National Party UNP) seeks legal opinion on the government's dissolution of local authorities, pending elections on March 27.
State attorney says there is an attempt to confuse the Presidential Commission investigating assassination of former senior UNP minister, Lalith Athulathmudali.
Denmark, Sweden, Norway and Finland to post attache in Sri Lanka, in a bid to prevent influx of bogus asylum sekers and illegal immigrants to these countries.

Ceylon Electricity Board Engineers claim government not willing to impose half-hourly power cuts with immediate effect, to conserve hydropower during drought. The board, the state-run monopoly power generator and distributor, however said at a recent press conference that adequate steps have been taken to tide over the January-May drought, using thermal power.
